newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks down on Wall Street, slim trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks down on Wall Street, slim trade.

text.p: Argentine stocks finished lower Monday, held back by a decline on Wall Street and slim volumes, but traders predicted the market could rise later in the week on a lack of U.S. indicator releases.
"The market was pressured by cautious investors who do not want to take out positions in the face of soft foreign markets," said Emilio Alessandro, an analyst at brokerage Alessandro y Compania.
The blue-chip Merval stock index fell 0.85 percent to 697.85 points, while the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange's general index slipped 0.46 percent.
Despite this marking the third consecutive session of declines, some said the market should firm this week.
"Prices should continue to rise," on the absence of key U.S. indicators to upset it this week, said Banco Credito in an investor note.
The expiration of options contracts at the end of last week should also free up the market to gain this week, said traders.
Activity fell to 15.5 million pesos from 19.5 million pesos Friday. Some 61 stocks were traded, with 31 decliners and 10 gainers. The rest were unchanged.
